rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for someone or something whose absence is felt, especially in a team or work context.

example.english: You not coming back to help is a real miss for our whole team.
example.traditional: 你唔返嚟幫手，對我哋成隊嚟講真係一個損失。
example.jyutping: nei5 m4 faan1 lai4 bong1 sau2 deoi3 ngo5 dei6 seng4 deoi6 lai4 gong2 zan1 hai6 jat1 go3 syun2 sat1

rows.note: Use 掛住 for the emotional sense of missing someone or something; it is the everyday choice in this territory.
Use 錯過 as the all-purpose choice when an event, opportunity, transport connection, or deadline is missed.

example.jyutping: ngo5 caa1 di1 co3 gwo3 baan1 ce1

rows.note: Use this physical-action pattern for failing to hit a target, as in 射唔中 or 打唔中.

example.jyutping: ngo5 se6 m4 zung3 go3 baa2

rows.note: Use 避開 when someone or something avoids being hit or narrowly escapes a collision.

example.english: The car nearly hit me, but luckily I miss getting hit.
example.traditional: 架車差啲撞到我，好彩我避開咗。
example.jyutping: gaa3 ce1 caa1 di1 zong6 dou2 ngo5 hou2 coi2 ngo5 bei6 hoi1 zo2
